cmad.notes: CMAD expected for operational NASA mission but not located. GOLD has no StopDate, is a NASA Heliophysics Explorer Mission of Opportunity, and was reviewed in the 2023 Heliophysics Senior Review (https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/final-2023-senior-review-report-tagged.pdf), whose GOLD section does not mention a CMAD. Searched: (a) no designated CMAD repository is configured; Zenodo searched anyway (no GOLD CMAD); (b) the GOLD Science Data Center documentation at UCF and the CDAWeb GOLD documentation directory (https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/sp_phys/data/gold/documentation/), which hold the Public Science Data Products Guide Rev 5.2 (January 2026), release notes, a data-issues table and a November 2026 notice, but no CMAD; (c) two web-search passes ('GOLD CMAD', 'GOLD Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document') returned only NASA's generic HPD CMAD template. The data products guide carries no front-page author list, so it was not treated as CMAD evidence. Current-team evidence came instead from the GOLD science team page.

external_roster: GOLD (far-ultraviolet imaging spectrograph, two identical independent channels A and B)
instrument_coverage.notes: Reverse lookup (registry.py lookup --observatory spase://SMWG/Observatory/GOLD, all authorities, 4512 of 4518 API-listed instruments read) found one Instrument record, spase://SMWG/Instrument/GOLD. The GOLD instrument page (read from the 11 August 2026 archived copy, https://web.archive.org/web/20260811204808/https://gold.cs.ucf.edu/science-mission/gold-instrument/, because the live UCF site returns an empty body to automated requests), the overview paper, the instrument design paper and the record's own Description all agree that GOLD is a single far-ultraviolet imaging spectrograph with two identical channels flown as a hosted payload on the commercial SES-14 satellite. The two channels are halves of one instrument, not separately described components, so no component entries were made. SES-14 carries no other NASA science payload. None missing from SPASE.

notes: Anchor paper: (Eastes et al. 2017, 10.1007/s11214-017-0392-2), 'The Global-Scale Observations of the Limb and Disk (GOLD) Mission', Space Science Reviews 212, 383. Selection confident: it names the mission in the title, has 25 authors, appeared online in 2016-2017 about a year before the 2018-01-25 operating-span start, is the most-cited GOLD paper (OpenAlex 223, Semantic Scholar 156, Crossref 129), and is the article the GOLD Instrument record itself links. OpenAlex, Crossref and Semantic Scholar give the same 25 authors in the same order. An earlier design-phase overview (Eastes et al. 2008, AGU Geophysical Monograph 181, 10.1029/181GM29) was considered and set aside as superseded.

Overview author-order analysis: the mechanical backward scan finds a sorted suffix of 6 (Aksnes ... Oberheide, positions 20-25), which would make positions 1-19 the prefix. But positions 4-19 (Anderson ... Woods) are themselves a 16-name alphabetical run, and the GOLD science team page shows why: the byline is PI (Eastes), Deputy PI (McClintock), Burns, then the Co-Investigators alphabetized, then the collaborators alphabetized. The deliberate prefix is therefore Eastes, McClintock, Burns (all Strong). Anderson and Andersson at positions 4-5 are alphabetical placement, not contribution order, so they were given no position-based Medium evidence (erring against position, as the procedure requires for ambiguous lists); they are included through the team page instead.

Instrument description paper: (McClintock et al. 2020, 10.1029/2020JA027797), 'GOLD Mission Implementation: 1. Instrument Design and Early Flight Performance'. Selection confident: instrument-design title, published two years after launch, OpenAlex, Crossref and Semantic Scholar agree on the 8 authors. Backward scan: suffix of 1, not alphabetized; positions 1-3 (McClintock, Eastes, Hoskins) taken at Strong; 4-5 (Siegmund, McPhate) recorded as GOLD-instrument Medium in instrument_roles; 6-8 (Krywonos, Solomon, Burns) carry no position evidence. The companion Part 2 paper (10.1029/2020JA027809, 16 authors) is partially alphabetized: sorted suffix of 14 from position 3 (Béland), prefix = McClintock, Eastes. It adds no new leads; its remaining alphabetized authors who are not evaluated elsewhere were not listed individually.

Literature-source agreement: OpenAlex (first), Crossref and Semantic Scholar agree on both author lists. Differences: Semantic Scholar dates the overview 2016 (online-first) where Crossref gives 2017-08-07 (issue); Crossref carries no ORCIDs for the 2017 paper, so ORCIDs come from OpenAlex; OpenAlex labels author 20 'ASMUND AKSNES' while Crossref has 'A. Aksnes' and the team page 'Dr. Arve Aksnes', so the OpenAlex given name is treated as a disambiguation error. SciX/ADS could not be queried (no API token in this environment; the ADS web UI is script-only), and Semantic Scholar keyword search was rate-limited (HTTP 429); its DOI lookups succeeded. NTRS was not needed.

Current-team source: the GOLD science team page at https://gold.cs.ucf.edu/science-mission/science-team/ returns HTTP 200 with an empty body to automated requests (WordPress REST API also refused, 401), so it was read from the Wayback Machine copy of 11 August 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260811204626/https://gold.cs.ucf.edu/science-mission/science-team/). Curator: confirm against the live page in a browser.

Eastes is recorded as PrincipalInvestigator of the mission (Observatory Contacts, team page, NASA 2018 release) and, in instrument_roles, as InstrumentLead of the GOLD instrument from the Instrument record Contacts. No current source names anyone else as instrument PI, so the Instrument-record role was kept as given. McClintock's DeputyPI role comes from mission-level sources, so it is in role_evidence but not in instrument_roles; because GOLD's mission and instrument are the same investigation, a curator may want DeputyPI on the Instrument record too.

Inclusion calls a curator may want to revisit: (1) the five team-page Collaborators (Aksnes, Budzien, Dymond, Eparvier, Oberheide) are included at Medium as overview-paper co-authors corroborated by the team page, though the page ranks them below the Co-Investigators; drop them as a block if the DOI should carry Co-Investigators and above only. (2) Sarah Jones (NASA GSFC Mission Scientist) is included with Author only, because 'Mission Scientist' has no SPASE role equivalent and the team page names Wenbin Wang separately as Project Scientist. (3) Andrey Krywonos is included as an overview co-author corroborated by his team-page Project Coordinator listing; that title on its own is not an author role. (4) Katelynn Greer is a current Co-Investigator with no authorship on either description paper. (5) Program Scientists Kozyra (current) and Talaat (at launch) are included at Medium per the ProgramScientist qualifying role.

Person-record matches: David N. Anderson left at null, but spase://SMWG/Person/D.Anderson ('Mr. D. Anderson', 'formerly at NOAA-SEL') may be him; verify downstream. Janet.U.Kozyra (University of Michigan) and Elsayed.Talaat (Applied Physics Laboratory) records carry their pre-NASA affiliations; they were linked because the names are distinctive. Wenbin.Wang (NCAR) linked; the GOLD team page gives UCAR. James E. Harvey was not linked to John.W.Harvey or any other Harvey record. Alan G. Burns, Alan C. Hoskins, Oswald Siegmund, Jerry Lumpe, Mihail Codrescu, Laila Andersson, Arthur Richmond, Carlos Martinis, Katelynn Greer, Sarah Jones and the collaborators have no SMWG Person record.

Name forms: the overview byline gives 'J. Harvey' (Photon Engineering) and the team page 'Dr. James Harvey, UCF/College of Optics and Photonics'; the 2008 monograph gives 'James E. Harvey', UCF CREOL, so they are treated as one person. 'Mr. Scott Evans' on the team page is J. Scott Evans of CPI.

Out-of-scope record observations for a curator: the Observatory record's ObservatoryRegion is Earth.Magnetosphere although GOLD images the thermosphere and ionosphere; its Description and InformationURLs mostly describe the SES-14 host satellite and still say GOLD is 'intended to perform a two-year mission' (the prime mission ended October 2020 and GOLD remains in extended operations). The Instrument record is InstrumentType Photometer for an imaging spectrograph, is still at SPASE 2.3.1, and links the mission overview paper rather than the 2020 instrument design paper.
